title: Sam Morgan's later years and his saxophonists
summary: Allen and Labat talk about Sam Morgan's stroke, Skeeter Fusche, Joe Harris and Tex.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Yeah, well I know he was good, even with what everybody says. You can tell it on the record but he must have been better, because he made that record in 1927 I think. And I think he'd already had one stroke at least or something. It's hard to tell what he was like. You know? Good. After he had that boy stroke he was dragging. Yeah, he was dragging. That's when he had Skeeter with him. Who's Skeeter? Well, Fusche. That's right. Red boy Alton. Alton. From Mobile, Alabama. I never will forget that. Because he's on Al Fusche. That's right. He's California now, isn't he? Is that right? I think he has a band and he's proud that he's got that Sam Morgan beat. Well. In California, I hear that. Well, I wish I knew what part of California he was like to write. Me too. Santa Barbara. Santa Barbara. Look, do you know he's an address there? No, but I think we could probably. He sacked him up there, wasn't he? Oh, Al Fusche. No, man. That's the man lying there. That's the man lying there. That's the man lying there. That's the man lying there. Every break I know, understand. Really? He learned you every break he knew? I used to go to the Oilers house at 10 o'clock every Sunday morning. And I don't care, sometimes I'd see him in the morning just going in, you see, when I'd be going to the grocery or something and I wouldn't go to his house. Do you know he'd call me up? He said, I don't care what time I come in, he said, I want somebody to play something like me. And I had to go every Sunday morning on Floyd Street. That's right. Third and that man lying there. Third and that man lying there.
Third and that man lying there.
Did he play around here much? With Sam Morgan. He come over with him. I see all of the coast, Buffaloes, Moabill, Sam Morgan and the rural all of that. Oh yeah.
What did you say he used to play over here with Joe Harris? Joe Harris. Joe Harris. He used good sax too, man. He used good sax. He was playing recently but I haven't seen him here.
He used to play with the Amethystogonians, man. He had a stroke.
He had a stroke. Yeah, I was fixing to say that.
He had a stroke. Yeah, I was fixing to say that. He had a stroke. He had a stroke.
I don't know Tex. Tex died in the cradle house, all right.
Tex is living. He had a stroke. He told me he died in the cradle house. He didn't die. He was sick.
Other part is all right but he didn't die.

I saw him at the bank with a couple of months or a meeting. Yeah. That Miles there we was trying to figure out what was Tess's name and I couldn't think of him. I knew him.
